title: KV block-chunking and GPU swap strategy for paged KV cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We are implementing a block-chunked paged KV cache that balances GPU residency, transfer overhead, and continuous-batching tail latency. This ticket captures the chosen on-GPU block layout, host/GPU swap strategy, allocator semantics, and pragmatic mitigations for observed GPU page thrashing under high-concurrency small requests.

Design decisions made so far:
- Block/chunk layout: fixed block size default=256KB; each block internally split into 4KB pages for fine-grained bookkeeping. Blocks are the unit of eviction/transfer to reduce CPU/GPU transfer call overhead.
- Allocator: free-list slab allocator per layer with coarse-grain defrag pass. New allocations prefer recent freed blocks to improve temporal locality.
- Residency tracking: per-request residency bitmap plus per-layer block LRU with frequency demotion. A block is considered "hot" if referenced in the last N batches (N=3 by default).
- Eviction policy: segmented LRU (hot/mid/cold), evict from cold first until GPU resident fraction < 0.85. Evicted blocks are asynchronously copied to pinned host memory (cudaHostAlloc) using a dedicated transfer CUDA stream to overlap with compute.
- Prefetching: when request traces show predictable prefix patterns we prefetch next-K blocks into GPU using a low-priority transfer queue.
- Throttle controls: global kv_transfer_rate_limit and per-stream concurrency caps to avoid saturating PCIe/NVLink and causing kernel stalls.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Why 256KB blocks? Benchmarks showed 256KB reduces the number of PCIe transfers by ~3x vs 64KB while keeping wasted copy volume acceptable. For many small requests (seq <= 64) 128KB gave slightly better p50 but worse p99 due to more frequent evictions; 256KB is a middle-ground for mixed traffic.
- Using pinned host memory (cudaHostAlloc) increases transfer throughput but raises host memory pressure; we allocate a bounded pinned pool per-node and fall back to pageable copies when the pool is exhausted.
- Async copy stream helps overlap work but requires careful synchronization of KV pointers and stream ordering; we use an epoch fence per-batch so that kernels never read a block until the transfer stream signals completion.
- Continuous batching interaction: with continuous batching there are frequent partial-KV writes (append-only across seq). We coalesce small writes into block-local staging buffers and flush at batch commit to reduce write amplification. This reduced p99 tail by ~32ms in our microbench for seq=1024.
- Observed thrash mode: many concurrent short requests that reference disjoint, interleaved KV positions caused repeated small transfers and pcie saturation. Mitigations: coalesce transfers per-batch, per-node transfer rate limiting, and a soft admission control that keeps very small requests on smaller-model fallback when system is overloaded.

Benchmarks (internal, 8xA100 node, mixed qps):
- Baseline (no block-chunking, eager full-KV resident): p99 latency (seq=1024) = 470ms; throughput = 1x.
- With block-chunking (256KB), pinned host eviction, async transfer: p99 = 320ms, throughput +12%, GPU memory fragmentation metric down 22%.
- Small-seq regime (seq<=64) with coalescing improvement: p99 down by 18ms vs naive chunking.

Open risks and follow-ups:
- cudaFree / driver interaction on pinned host pool exhaustion caused transient OOMs on one test cluster. Need driver-level defensive tests and fallback path to pageable memory.
- Multi-GPU path: when a request spans KV on two GPUs we currently serialize transfers through host; evaluate NVLink GPUDirect or peer-copy to eliminate host round-trip.
- Eviction correctness for function-calling tool outputs (structured outputs that reference past KV positions). Add integration e2e tests.

notes: Avoid using very small block sizes (<64KB) in mixed workloads; causes transfer overhead and tail spikes.
Consider later adding predictive eviction using simple LSTM on request traces if heuristics are insufficient.
Customer opt-out flag: runtime.kv_paging.enabled = false for customers who want thin-client behavior
